title.value: REAL-M: TOWARDS SPEECH SEPARATION ON REAL MIXTURES
title.justification: The direct title of the paper is provided in the document.
title.quote: REAL-M: TOWARDS SPEECH SEPARATION ON REAL MIXTURES

extractions.description: The paper discusses the development of REAL-M, a dataset of real-life mixtures for speech separation. It introduces a blind neural SI-SNR estimator for evaluating separated speech signal quality. The estimator correlates well with human assessments and is tested on popular speech separation models.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on speech separation and the development of tools for evaluating speech separation models on real mixtures, without a direct link to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper addresses the problem from a different angle and provides a two-fold contribution. First, we release REAL-M, a real-life speech source separation dataset for two-speaker mixtures. Secondly, we design and study a neural network that blindly estimates the quality of a signal processed by a speech separation model.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any specific themes that align with Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: The vast majority of studies in the field employ synthetic datasets for both training and evaluation purposes.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to sustainable development; the focus is purely on audio and speech separation advancements.
secondary_categories.quote: We collected this dataset through crowdsourcing by asking contributors to read a predefined set of sentences simultaneously.

primary_sub_category.justification: There are no sub-categories that match the focus of the paper, which is on technical advancements in speech separation.
primary_sub_category.quote: The main challenge that prevents evaluating real-life mixtures is the lack of ground truth signals (i.e., the clean sources used as targets for training and evaluating speech separation).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories of sustainable development are addressed here as the topic is entirely technical on speech separation.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: As humans, we can tell if the quality of a speech signal is good or not just by listening to it. By following this reasoning, we describe here how we designed a neural network that estimates the separation performance.

applications.justification: The paper's main contribution revolves around improving speech separation techniques for real-world applications, a purely technical focus.
applications.quote: In recent years, deep learning-based source separation has achieved impressive results. Most studies, however, still evaluate separation models on synthetic datasets, while the performance of state-of-the-art techniques on in-the-wild speech data remains an open question.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing sustainable development categories do not apply to this paper, which is focused on speech separation technology.
new_primary_category.quote: This paper contributes to fill this gap in two ways. First, we release the REAL-M dataset, a crowd-sourced corpus of real-life mixtures.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: As there is no link to sustainable development, proposing a new sub-category is unnecessary.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The basic components needed to train the neural SI-SNR estimator are a pretrained separation model, a synthetic dataset, and a neural network for SI-SNR estimation.
